card_a: “I don’t have a family history, so I’m not at risk.”
card_b: Family history is one of many risk factors. Anyone can develop breast cancer.
explanation: Family history can increase risk, but about 80% of breast cancers occur in women with no specific risk factors other than sex and age.
source_name: World Health Organization — Breast cancer fact sheet

card_b: Many changes are not cancer, but new or persistent ones should be checked.
explanation: Most breast lumps are harmless, such as cysts or fibroadenomas. A healthcare professional can check any new or persistent lump.

card_a: “Screening recommendations are the same for everyone.”
card_b: Screening depends on age, risk factors and medical history. Ask a professional.
explanation: When and how often to screen depends on your age and personal risk. Talk with a healthcare professional about what suits you.
source_name: National Cancer Institute — Mammograms fact sheet

card_b: Men can develop breast cancer too.
explanation: Men have breast tissue too. Breast cancer is much less common in men, but it can happen, usually at an older age.
source_name: National Cancer Institute — Male Breast Cancer (Patient Version)

card_b: Noticing a change early and getting advice can lead to better outcomes.
explanation: Deaths are reduced when breast cancer is detected and treated early. If you notice a change, getting advice sooner helps.
source_name: World Health Organization — Breast cancer fact sheet

card_b: Know what is normal for you.
explanation: Learning what is normal for your body makes it easier to notice something new.

card_b: A change doesn't always mean cancer, but noticed changes are worth checking with a healthcare professional.
explanation: Most changes are not cancer, but a healthcare professional can tell you what a change means.

card_b: You are not alone. A kind conversation can encourage someone to seek help.
explanation: Support matters. Listening without judgement and encouraging a friend to see a professional can make a real difference.

card_b: Your health matters. Make time for regular check-ups and healthy habits.
explanation: Taking care of yourself includes regular check-ups and everyday habits like staying active.
